questions.q: Per this lesson, what is the typical system of record for employee master data?
options: Whichever department last updated the record
The HR system (HRIS)
The vendor master system
The customer relationship management (CRM) system
questions.explain: Employee master data overwhelmingly originates from one place, the HR system, rather than dozens of inconsistent external touchpoints.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say employee master usually has less of a matching-and-deduplication burden than customer master?
options: Because employee records don't require any governance at all
Because employee data is never referenced by other domains
Because employees never change jobs or departments
Because it comes from a single authoritative source (HR) rather than many inconsistent external touchpoints
questions.explain: With one point of entry, the data doesn't arrive duplicated and inconsistent the way customer data does from many unrelated external channels — the harder problem becomes keeping downstream systems in sync.

questions.q: What attributes does a location master record typically hold, according to this lesson?
options: The names of every employee who has ever worked at that site
A unique location code, address, geocode, and type-specific operational attributes
Only a store's weekly sales total
A list of every vendor invoice processed there
questions.explain: A location record identifies the site itself — code, address, geocode, type (warehouse, store, office) — and attributes relevant to that type, like a warehouse's storage capacity.

questions.q: What practical consequence does this lesson give for a location record with a stale or wrong address?
options: It has no real consequence beyond an outdated mailing label
It automatically triggers the closure of that location
It can misroute a shipment or cause tax calculations to use the wrong jurisdiction
It only affects the company's internal phone directory
questions.explain: Shipping and logistics systems route by location code, and tax engines often need an accurate location (sometimes down to the geocode) to apply the correct jurisdiction's rate.

questions.q: How do employee and location master connect to the other domains discussed in this chapter?
options: They appear as attributes inside other domains, such as a customer's account manager being an employee ID or a vendor's dock being a location code
They replace the need for customer and vendor master entirely
They can only be used for internal reporting, never referenced elsewhere
They are entirely separate systems with no links to customer, product, or vendor master
questions.explain: Because these domains are referenced from within other master records, governance treats the whole set as one connected system — a broken reference in one domain propagates wherever it's referenced.
